findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a rollback/escape path for false-positive probe failures: at minimum name the opt-in flag and document it in the error message emitted under outcome 3, so operators can unblock themselves without a code change.
evidence: Approach outcome 3: 'Remote unreachable / probe times out → REFUSE (fail closed)' — the probe is new logic with its own failure modes.
ABSENCE: No back-out plan, feature flag, or expand-contract sequence is described for the case where the ls-remote probe itself misbehaves post-deployment.
The opt-in flag is referenced as the escape hatch but is entirely unspecified, making it unavailable as a documented rollback path.
findings.finding: The plan's fail-closed behavioral change (non-zero exit where previously init silently succeeded) is an acknowledged breaking change, but the plan provides no rollback or back-out mechanism for the probe logic itself. The opt-in flag is the intended safety valve, yet it is unspecified (see E1 finding), so operators have no concrete recourse if the ls-remote probe introduces false-positive 'unreachable' failures in a production environment (e.g., proxy environments where ls-remote behaves differently than clone).
findings.location: Approach section — outcome 3; Files section
scenarios: ls-remote probe returns non-zero due to proxy/firewall config in an environment where the outer clone succeeded; init now refuses where it previously worked; operators have no documented flag to pass because it is unnamed.
A git server that responds slowly to ls-remote (but not to clone) triggers the timeout, causing false-positive refuses with no operator escape.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit in the outcome-3 error message: 'Remote could not be reached within Xs. If you are certain this is a genuine first-init, re-run with --force-bootstrap to override.' This makes the flag self-documenting and provides a concrete back-out path without requiring a code rollback.

findings.finding: AC4 tests the opt-in flag only against an unreachable remote (case 3 → bootstrap), but no AC tests what happens when the opt-in flag is passed alongside a reachable remote that advertises the tickets branch (case 1). The flag's interaction with case 1 is a material failure path of the new flag feature that the test plan leaves uncovered.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py` (lines 100 and 237) as an affected consumer of `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, and explicitly specify whether the ls-remote probe lives inside that predicate (touching the hot pre-command path) or only inside `_mount_or_create_branch` (keeping the predicate local-only and fast).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_init.py:100 — 'if _init_cmd.pending_init_attaches_to_existing(repo_root):'

src/rebar/_cli/_init.py:237 — 'if _init_cmd.pending_init_is_symlink(root) or _init_cmd.pending_init_attaches_to_existing(root):' in the best-effort pre-command mount that must 'never hang, never raise'
Plan Files section lists only 'src/rebar/_commands/init.py, tests' — _cli/_init.py is absent.

AC7: 'pending_init_attaches_to_existing returns True when the remote advertises tickets even though the local remote-tracking ref is absent' — this semantic change directly affects both _cli/_init.py call sites.
findings.finding: src/rebar/_cli/_init.py is an unenumerated consumer of pending_init_attaches_to_existing (called at lines 100 and 237) that lies outside the plan's stated edit boundary (_commands/init.py + tests). The line-237 call is on a pre-command hot path whose documented contract is 'never hang, never raise, never first-time-init'; if the plan's ls-remote probe is wired into pending_init_attaches_to_existing (as AC7 implies), every CLI invocation that triggers that path will incur bounded network I/O — contrary to the caller's contract and unacknowledged in the plan.
findings.location: Files section / AC7 ('pending_init_attaches_to_existing returns True when the remote advertises tickets…')
scenarios: Every rebar CLI subcommand invocation hits _cli/_init.py:237's best-effort mount; if pending_init_attaches_to_existing now calls ls-remote with a non-trivial timeout, all commands incur that latency even when the store is already mounted.

If ls-remote raises or times out in the _cli/_init.py:237 path, the broad except swallows it silently — the auto-attach silently fails, leaving the store unmounted with no diagnostic, violating the intent of the fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the ls-remote probe to _mount_or_create_branch only. Keep pending_init_attaches_to_existing checking only local refs (rev-parse). The AC7 predicate test can be satisfied by a separate, fast probe helper that _mount_or_create_branch calls before orphan-bootstrapping. This preserves the 'never hang' contract of the _cli/_init.py pre-command path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a concrete default probe timeout (e.g. 15 s) and whether it is configurable (e.g. via a `REBAR_REMOTE_PROBE_TIMEOUT` env var or `sync.probe_timeout` config key), so AC-3's 'names the timeout' contract is testable and the implementer is not guessing.
evidence: Plan states: 'The probe must be bounded so case 3 fails fast rather than hanging init' — no value given.

The ticket's root-cause comment notes: 'git fetch origin tickets was killed at 100s and at the 120s tool limit, but completed successfully in several minutes' — a probe timeout that is too short would misclassify this as unreachable.
run_git() in src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:32 accepts a timeout parameter, so the mechanism exists; the policy value is the missing piece.
findings.finding: The plan says the ls-remote probe 'must be bounded' and AC-3 says the error message must 'name the timeout', but no specific timeout value or configuration mechanism is given anywhere in the plan. For the P1 environment (slow agent git proxy, 49k-commit history), an implementer choosing a value that is too short will produce false-unreachable failures on a healthy but slow remote; too long re-introduces the hanging-init failure mode.
findings.location: Approach section — 'The probe must be bounded so case 3 fails fast'; AC-3 — 'message distinct from case 1 that names the timeout'
scenarios: Implementer picks 15s; a healthy but proxy-slowed remote consistently times out → all init attempts refuse with 'unreachable' even though the remote is fine, breaking AC-1 and AC-6.
Implementer picks 120s; a truly unreachable blackholed endpoint hangs for two minutes before failing fast — AC-3's 'bounded time' requirement is not met.

findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'The ls-remote probe runs with a 15 s timeout (configurable via `REBAR_PROBE_TIMEOUT` env var, default 15). The error message for case 3 includes the numeric value: "remote <name> did not respond within 15s".'

findings.finding: The plan's Approach section, AC3, and the upstream ticket comment give three mutually inconsistent behaviors for the 'unreachable remote' case: the Approach implies orphan-bootstrap is allowed only when the remote 'genuinely has no such branch' (unreachable ≠ no branch → should fail?); AC3 says 'fails within a bounded time' (implying non-zero exit for unreachable); but the ticket's root-cause comment says 'unreachable warns and keeps orphan-bootstrap so offline first-time init still works.' An implementer cannot derive a single correct behavior from these three statements, and the wrong choice here (fail-closed on unreachable when there is no prior tracking ref) will break legitimate offline first-inits on repos with a configured remote.
findings.location: Approach section / AC3 / ticket comment (1cb6-d553 / 01e8-302b comment by RebarBotNava)
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the Approach with: 'An unreachable remote (ls-remote probe times out or connection refused) is treated as indeterminate — init emits a warning naming the remote and proceeds to orphan-bootstrap, since the alternative (fail-closed) would break offline first-inits. AC3 should be rephrased: "With an unreachable remote, init exits within a bounded time (warning emitted, bootstrap proceeds) rather than hanging indefinitely."' Only the case where the remote is reachable AND advertises the tickets branch should be fail-closed.

findings.finding: No acceptance criterion covers the case where the remote is reachable but the probe fails for a non-reachability reason (e.g., SSH auth failure, HTTP 403, permission denied). In this case the probe may return a non-zero exit code or empty output indistinguishable from 'branch does not exist,' causing the new logic to silently bootstrap an orphan — reproducing the original P1 bug for a common operational scenario.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — missing AC for probe-error (auth/permission failure)
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'When the remote is reachable but the probe returns an authentication/permission error (simulated via a remote requiring credentials the caller does not have), init exits non-zero, names the remote and the error, and creates no orphan branch (`git branch --list tickets` empty). Tier: CLI subprocess.'

findings.finding: The probe's failure modes beyond timeout and 'branch absent' are unspecified: if the remote-probe command (e.g., `git ls-remote`) exits with an unexpected error (auth failure, DNS partial resolution, malformed output), the plan does not state whether init should fail closed, fail open, or surface a distinct error — leaving an ambiguous partial-state path.
findings.location: Approach section: 'probe the configured remote. If it is reachable and advertises the configured tickets branch, refuse to bootstrap'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a default 'fail closed on any probe error other than confirmed branch-absent' rule to the Approach section, and add a brief AC: 'Any unexpected probe error (e.g., auth failure) also fails non-zero and does not bootstrap.'

findings.finding: The plan's approach describes a binary probe outcome (reachable-and-advertises-branch vs. genuinely-no-branch) but does not specify the behavior when the probe itself encounters an error state — e.g., an authentication failure, a partial-connectivity error, or a git transport error that is neither 'remote reachable and branch found' nor 'clean unreachable'. Without a specified and tested behavior for this third state, the implementation may inadvertently treat a probe error as 'no such branch' and silently proceed with orphan-bootstrap, reproducing the original P1 defect under a different trigger.
findings.location: Approach section + Acceptance Criteria (no AC covers probe-error third state)
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit AC: 'When the remote probe exits non-zero for a reason other than an empty branch list (e.g., auth failure, transport error), init fails closed with a non-zero exit and an informative error message.' In the Approach section, clarify: treat any probe error that is not a clean empty-branch-list as a failure-closed condition, not as a legitimate first-init trigger.
